record.paper_title: Ultra-Dense Cell-Free Massive MIMO for 6G: Technical Overview and Open Questions
record.context_brief: Choice of centralized, local, or hybrid processing
record.original_question: What user-centric signal-processing design should an ultra-dense cell-free massive multiple-input multiple-output (CF-MMIMO) system use for uplink combining and downlink precoding when the alternatives include centralized processing at central processing units (CPUs), local processing at each access point (AP), and cluster-level combinations that trade spectral efficiency, fronthaul traffic, CPU computational load, robustness to AP additions or failures, and support for multiple-antenna APs?

evidence.quote: B. What User-Centric Processing Should Ultra-Dense Cell-Free Massive MIMO Use?
In Section IV, we described a general user-centric CF-MMIMO system where the signal processing, including UL combining and DL precoding, can be done centrally at the CPUs or locally at each AP.

In summary, local processing stands out as an ideal choice for ultra-dense CF-MMIMO systems. It provides an excellent balance between the computational complexity, system resilience, and system performance.
The remaining challenge in implementing this approach is the necessity for a flexible fronthaul infrastructure capable of dynamically routing fronthaul traffic among dynamic clusters.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider an ultra-dense cell-free massive multiple-input multiple-output (CF-MMIMO) wireless network consisting of a large number of geographically distributed access points (APs), each possibly equipped with multiple antennas, connected via a fronthaul network to one or more central processing units (CPUs), and jointly serving a set of single-antenna user equipments (UEs) on the same time-frequency resource. Each UE k is served by a user-centric cluster M_k of nearby APs. For the uplink, the signal received at AP l from UE k passes through a channel h_{kl} estimated locally; the system must form a combined estimate of the transmitted symbol. For the downlink, the system must compute precoding vectors w_{kl} for each AP l in M_k. The following three architectures are available:

(i) Fully centralized processing: APs forward all received pilot and data samples to a CPU, which performs channel estimation, uplink combining (e.g., MMSE) and downlink precoding jointly across all APs.

(ii) Fully local (distributed) processing: each AP estimates channels locally and computes its own combining/precoding vectors (e.g., local MMSE or maximum-ratio), forwarding only soft symbol estimates or precoded signals over the fronthaul.

(iii) Hybrid cluster-level processing: APs are grouped into clusters; processing is centralized within each cluster and decentralized between clusters.

For each architecture one can quantify: per-UE spectral efficiency (uplink and downlink), aggregate fronthaul traffic (bits/s on each fronthaul link), CPU computational load (floating point operations per coherence block), robustness to dynamic addition or failure of individual APs, and ability to exploit multi-antenna APs.

Problem: Determine the user-centric uplink combining rule and downlink precoding rule, together with the choice among centralized, local, or hybrid cluster-level processing, that should be adopted in an ultra-dense CF-MMIMO system so as to achieve the most favorable joint trade-off among spectral efficiency, fronthaul traffic, CPU computational complexity, resilience to AP additions/failures, and support for multiple-antenna APs. In particular, characterize whether a single architecture dominates the others in this multi-objective sense and, if not, identify the operational regimes (in terms of AP density, cluster size, fronthaul capacity, and number of AP antennas) in which each architecture is preferred.
artifact.status_search_result: The choice between centralized, local, and cluster-level processing in ultra-dense cell-free massive MIMO remains an active open research problem. Recent surveys and research papers from 2024–2026 continue to investigate the trade-offs and propose new distributed and hybrid schemes, with no consensus that a single architecture dominates across all metrics.

status_evidence.snippet: Studies scalable signal processing variants for cell-free massive MIMO showing different trade-offs between centralized and distributed implementations.
status_evidence.claim: The trade-off between centralized and distributed processing in CF-MMIMO remains an active research topic with no universally dominant scheme.
